prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val] Extreme · 10 columns + unbreakable values (language en).
Grid: 10 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "ID" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 16px
  col 2: header "SKU" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 136px
  col 3: header "Color" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 4: header "Size" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 31px
  col 5: header "Qty" · longest unbreakable word 26px · one-line width 26px
  col 6: header "Price" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
  col 7: header "Tax" · longest unbreakable word 32px · one-line width 32px
  col 8: header "Total" · longest unbreakable word 47px · one-line width 47px
  col 9: header "Warehouse" · longest unbreakable word 81px · one-line width 122px
  col 10: header "Tracking" · longest unbreakable word 159px · one-line width 159px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 720px. You MAY choose a total wider than 719px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Show order line items with product variants, quantities, charges, warehouse locations, and shipment tracking.","reading":"Readers scan each row from product identification through quantity and charges to fulfillment details, and compare quantities and amounts down their columns. Wrapping can make rows taller, so keeping related values aligned within each row matters.","groups":["ID and SKU identify the line and product.","Color and Size describe the product variant.","Qty, Price, Tax, and Total support comparison of quantities and charges.","Warehouse and Tracking describe fulfillment and shipment."],"keep_intact":["Column headers should remain whole.","Quantities, prices, tax, and totals should each stay on one line.","Tracking identifiers should preferably stay intact; if split, they must remain inside their cells.","SKU segments should remain intact where possible."],"may_wrap":["SKU values can wrap at hyphens, though excessive lines make comparison harder.","Warehouse names can wrap at hyphens; their wrapping can share row height already created by SKU or tracking."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [38, 57, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 102, 180] · table 721×402px · row heights [36, 106, 129, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/10 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 6 · OVERFLOWS the box by 1px
Design r0B: widths [38, 110, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 102, 127] · table 721×216px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/10 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 2 · OVERFLOWS the box by 1px
Design r0C: widths [38, 157, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 102, 180] · table 821×216px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/10 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 101px
Constraint adjustments applied: r0A: raised a column to the minimum 38px
r0B: raised a column to the minimum 38px
r0C: raised a column to the minimum 38px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
